questions.stem: Which of the following is a case of inverse proportion?
choices: Number of workers and time to complete a job
Time and distance at uniform speed
Area of land and crop harvested
Number of hours and number of workers
questions.solution: The number of workers on a job and the time to complete the job is an example of inverse proportion because more workers reduce the time required to finish the job. The other options are either direct proportions or not related proportionally.

questions.stem: What is the condition for two quantities to be in inverse proportion?
choices: If one quantity increases, the other decreases and vice versa
If the product of the quantities is not constant
questions.solution: The correct answer is that if one quantity increases, the other decreases and vice versa. This is the definition of inverse proportion. The other options are incorrect because they describe direct proportion or do not satisfy the condition of inverse proportion. The product of the quantities must remain constant in inverse proportion, not vary.

questions.stem: If the cost of 1 kg of sugar is 36, what would be the cost of 3 kg of sugar?
questions.solution: The cost of 1 kg of sugar is 36, so the cost of 3 kg of sugar is 3 times that, which is 108. The option '72' is incorrect because it adds 36 twice instead of thrice. The option '36' is incorrect because it assumes the cost remains the same for 3 kg. The option '18' is incorrect because it divides instead of multiplies.

questions.stem: If 5 workers can complete a job in 10 days, how many days will it take for 10 workers to complete the same job?

questions.stem: If 3 persons can rewire a house in 4 days, how many days will it take for 4 persons to complete the job?
questions.solution: This is an inverse proportion problem. If 3 persons take 4 days, then 4 persons will take (3 * 4) / 4 = 3 days. The other options do not correctly apply the inverse proportion relationship.

hi.solution: यह एक व्युत्क्रम समानुपात की समस्या है। यदि 3 व्यक्ति 4 दिन लेते हैं, तो 4 व्यक्ति (3 × 4) / 4 = 3 दिन लेंगे। अन्य विकल्प व्युत्क्रम समानुपात के संबंध को सही तरीके से लागू नहीं करते हैं।

questions.stem: If 5 metres of cloth cost ₹210, what is the cost of 2 metres of cloth?
questions.solution: To find the cost of 2 metres of cloth, first determine the cost per metre by dividing ₹210 by 5, which gives ₹42 per metre. Then multiply ₹42 by 2 to get ₹84. The other options are incorrect because they do not follow this proportional calculation. ₹105, ₹126, and ₹168 do not result from correctly applying the unit price to 2 metres.

questions.stem: A farmer has food for 20 animals for 6 days. If 10 more animals are added, how many days will the food last?
questions.solution: This is an inverse proportion problem. The total food is enough for 20 * 6 = 120 animal-days. With 30 animals, it will last 120 / 30 = 4 days. The other options do not correctly apply the inverse proportion relationship.

hi.stem: एक किसान के पास 20 पशुओं के लिए 6 दिन के भोजन के लिए भोजन है। यदि 10 अतिरिक्त पशु जोड़ दिए जाएं, तो भोजन कितने दिन तक रहेगा?
hi.solution: यह एक व्युत्क्रम समानुपात की समस्या है। कुल भोजन 20 × 6 = 120 पशु-दिन के लिए पर्याप्त है। 30 पशुओं के साथ, यह 120 / 30 = 4 दिन तक रहेगा। अन्य विकल्प व्युत्क्रम समानुपात के संबंध को सही ढंग से लागू नहीं करते हैं।

questions.stem: If the petrol consumption of a car is 4 litres for 60 km, and then increases to 12 litres, what is the relationship between petrol consumption and distance travelled?
questions.solution: Petrol consumption and distance travelled are directly proportional because as one increases, the other also increases in the same ratio. The option 'Inversely proportional' is incorrect because it implies that as one increases, the other decreases. The option 'No relation' is incorrect because there is a clear relationship. The option 'Partially proportional' is incorrect because the relationship is fully proportional.

questions.stem: If the speed of a vehicle doubles, what happens to the time taken to cover a fixed distance?
